text:
matt: Hey team — customer 'acme-prod' hitting intermittent 403s when the private-agent pulls model shards and when their app hits /v1/models in our registry. Only fails from inside their VPC behind a corporate proxy/NAT. Repro steps and logs below.

matt: logs:
```
2026-03-16T14:02:03Z agent: fetch shard https://shards.redwood-cdn.com/abc123 -> status=403
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 403
```
Also: `curl -v https://registry.redwood.ai/v1/models/mdl-xyz -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` shows TLS handshake then HTTP 403.

danielle: Thanks — can you repro from a bastion inside their VPC? My gut says DNS split-horizon or TLS MITM (corporate TLS inspection). If MITM, we need SNI passthrough/bypass for our hosts.

matt: Repro'd from their bastion. `curl -v --resolve registry.redwood.ai:443:10.0.1.12 https://registry.redwood.ai/v1/models/mdl-xyz` -> 200.
Without `--resolve` it fails 403. So DNS is resolving to an internal VIP (10.0.1.12) which looks like the proxy.

raj: If --resolve fixes it then the proxy is terminating TLS or rewriting Host/SNI. We should provide a minimal allowlist and explicit advice to disable TLS interception for our hosts. Minimal hosts I request from customers:
```
registry.redwood.ai:443
models.redwood.ai:443
shards.redwood-cdn.com:443
telemetry.redwood.ai:443
auth.redwood.ai:443
pypi.org:443
files.pythonhosted.org:443
github.com:443
ocsp.digicert.com:80,443
ocsp.globalsign.com:80,443
*.redwood-cdn.com:443
```
Also note: OCSP/CRL/responder access is required for certificate validation — allow outbound to well-known OCSP URLs. If customer uses an internal KMS for signing keys, add `kms.*.amazonaws.com:443`.

danielle: +1. Also include a note: do NOT rewrite Host headers or strip SANs; ensure SNI passthrough for `registry.redwood.ai` and the shard hostnames. If TLS inspection cannot be disabled, they must at least add an exclusion list for those hostnames so the connection is end-to-end. :warning:

matt: They reported pip/wheel downloads also failing with `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER]` — that usually means the proxy is returning plain HTTP on port 443 (middlebox). Customer uses BlueCoat inline TLS inspect.

support: For triage, ask them to run these commands from their bastion and paste outputs: 
- `dig registry.redwood.ai +short`
- `curl -vI https://registry.redwood.ai/`
- `openssl s_client -connect <resolved-ip>:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai -showcerts`
- `curl -vL https://shards.redwood-cdn.com/abc123 -H "Range: bytes=0-1023"`
These will show if the cert CN/SAN matches and if the server is returning redirects to external CDNs.

infra-bot: Internal KB: https://intra.redwood.ai/kb/egress-allowlist-private — includes recommended host list, OCSP note, and sample ip/cidr hints. Add note that model shards may redirect to third-party CDNs (Akamai/Fastly) so wildcard allowlist for `*.redwood-cdn.com` or collecting `curl -I` redirect host is needed.

raj: Additional tip: model shard downloads use range requests and sometimes temporary signed URLs. The redirect chain can include `storage.googleapis.com` or `edge-*` hosts. If customers can't wildcard, have them capture the `Location` header from a failing `curl -I` and add that host.

danielle: Action items: I'll assemble an official allowlist + TLS-bypass checklist and send to acme-sre. Matt — can you paste the outputs (dig + openssl) here? I'll include them in the KB example.

matt: Pasting quick outputs (bastion):
```
$ dig registry.redwood.ai +short
10.0.1.12

$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.1.12:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = proxy.corp.local
---
subject=CN = proxy.corp.local
issuer=CN = Internal-CA
---
```
So the cert is `proxy.corp.local` — confirms TLS interception/MITM.

danielle: Perfect repro, thanks. I'll follow up with the KB and the allowlist doc and request their infra team to add SNI bypass for `registry.redwood.ai` and `*.redwood-cdn.com`.

matt: Sending KB + sample allowlist to customer now. Will update if they report any remaining 403s. :white_check_mark:
